prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, from heterobifunctional PROTACs to the molecular basis of cereblon-directed molecular glues

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is the one candidate that every member ranked, and the breadth of that support is backed by substance rather than by habit. Crews and Deshaies established the heterobifunctional concept and showed it working in cells. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target gave a molecular explanation for a drug action that had been a mystery for decades. Together these define a new chemical modality, not a single reaction. From a structural viewpoint, the field is also unusually well evidenced: crystal structures of ternary complexes show how a degrader brings ligase and target together, so the mechanism rests on determined structures and not on inference. Many independent groups have reproduced the work, and clinical-stage degraders and approved cereblon-based drugs exist. In my opening ballot I put perovskites first. After reading my colleagues, I now judge that the stronger case for the 2026 prize is the one that can be defended on mechanism, attribution and breadth at once.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC has yet been approved, so the clinical proof for the heterobifunctional branch is still pending. The credited list is long (Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Kim and Ito), and a three-person limit leaves out Ciulli, whose VHL ligand and ternary-complex crystallography made the field rational. The prize could also be read as pharmacology and chemical biology more than chemistry, and the concept may be only a few years from a clearer clinical verdict. If the committee judges that waiting is wiser, halide perovskites are the stronger materials case and are where my own judgement of designed structure leading to function applies most directly.

responses.point: Chabes ranks targeted protein degradation first because induced proximity gives a general catalytic tool for removing any chosen protein, and the cereblon work finally explains thalidomide mechanistically.
responses.response: I agree on the mechanism and have moved toward your position since my opening. I would add that the strongest evidence for the claim is structural, in the ternary-complex crystal structures. That is why I am unhappy that Ciulli is left out of the three-person set. I still think the claim of an explained mechanism is stronger for the cereblon and molecular-glue branch than for PROTACs, where design rules are still empirical. I also disagree mildly that the absence of an approved PROTAC is a minor point. It is the reason I would put the citation weight on induced proximity and cereblon, not on clinical outcomes.

responses.point: Linke places nanopore sequencing first as a clean physical principle turned into a mature analytical capability, and ranks halide perovskites second for their rapid efficiency gains and broad optoelectronic reach.
responses.response: I share your view that perovskites are a physically understandable family with generative reach, and I ranked them first on my opening ballot. My reservations are attribution and maturity. Six credited names, with Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis all having strong claims, make a clean three-person split harder than for protein degradation. Operational stability and lead content are unresolved after a decade, so I cannot call it settled in the way I can call the nanopore case settled. On nanopores, I accept the maturity argument, but the three-person configuration separates the idea of threading a polynucleotide through a channel from the engineering that made it work. I am not yet convinced that this separation is clean, and Branton and Kasianowicz would have to be justified as omissions.

responses.point: Aili ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles first as a clear case of molecular design that enabled siRNA and mRNA medicines, and notes the complementarity with the 2023 Medicine prize.
responses.response: The societal impact is beyond question and I take the complementarity argument seriously. My concern is the attribution you flag yourself. Six credited people, with Cullis, Madden, Hope and MacLachlan in Vancouver and Anderson and Langer elsewhere, and no agreed account of which step was decisive. A prize that has to omit Hope or Langer, or both, is on weaker ground than one with a more compact credit. I would also ask for the structural and mechanistic evidence that the pKa-driven endosomal-escape model is established and not plausible, and your ballot does not settle that for me.

responses.point: Somfai ranks palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling first, as a general and practical method that is routine in medicinal and process chemistry and was left out of the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
responses.response: I agree that Buchwald and Hartwig form a natural pair and that the maturity is not in doubt. My hesitation is the novelty relative to 2010. The committee has already recognised palladium cross-coupling as a concept, and I worry that a C-N prize would be read as completing that earlier prize, whereas induced proximity opens a new modality. That is a judgement of degree, not a decisive point, and I would not oppose B016 if the committee prefers a mature, broadly used method.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks proton-coupled electron transfer first as a physically stated mechanistic concept with theory, model systems and decades of confirmation, and ranks nitrogenase third.
responses.response: I accept that proton-coupled electron transfer is mature and mechanistically rigorous. My question is whether it is one achievement. You separate the theory (Hammes-Schiffer), the thermochemistry (Mayer) and the model systems (Nocera) and also leave out Meyer. That reads as a field with several contributions and no single decisive one, so the citation would be hard to write. On nitrogenase we agree on Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt. I still see the structure as established and the mechanism as unresolved, which is why I keep it as an alternative and not as a lead.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept the absence of an approved PROTAC drug, or prefer to wait for clinical proof.
How to credit Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Kim and Ito when only three names fit, and whether Handa should be preferred over Ciulli.
Whether the attribution difficulty and stability concerns for halide perovskites (Grätzel, Seok, Kanatzidis) can be resolved into a defensible three-person set.
Whether the first-principles mechanism of cereblon-directed degradation is established well enough in structural terms to carry the molecular-glue half of the citation.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I am a Stockholm University colleague of the Secretary, Peter Brzezinski, but none of the shortlisted candidates is connected to him or to me through collaboration or institution, so no recusal is needed.
